title: Define profile questions and decision taxonomy
description: Turn the agreed product direction into a decision framework before specifying UI or metrics. Define what 'What does my collection reveal about me?' and 'What deserves my attention or a decision now?' mean in concrete user terms. Enumerate legitimate responses such as play/replay, keep/remove, correct a rating or model, recognize an intentional exception, and change future buying. Distinguish stable identity, model diagnostics, unresolved collection choices, and mere statistics. Audit current and candidate signals against those jobs without assuming they should survive.
acceptance_criteria: The artifact names the user questions and decision categories; each category includes the unresolved condition, evidence required, plausible user responses, and reasons to abstain; current axis distributions, Tournament divergence, collection outliers, prediction misses, neglect/play history, redundancy, and purchase utilization are evaluated as retain, drilldown, redesign, remove, or unresolved; no signal is retained solely because it is computable or statistically defensible; the result is sufficient input for a product specification and records open owner decisions rather than hiding them in implementation details.
notes: Conversation handoff (2026-08-28): The owner confirmed the profile must answer exactly two top-level questions: (1) What does my collection reveal about me? (2) What deserves my attention or a decision now? The previous Trusted Collection Insights work improved evidentiary integrity but did not demonstrate usefulness; do not continue by adding more evidence or statistics. Axis distributions are specifically useful because they let the owner verify whether configured axes are being used as expected. Tournament-value-versus-fitness divergence is specifically considered not useful and should not be preserved by default. Rating/prediction residuals may be interesting because they can ask whether a game is an intentional exception or the model misunderstands the owner, but this is only a candidate and must prove a user response. A profile attention item is actionable only when it identifies an unresolved choice, not merely a threshold crossing. Candidate decision families discussed: play/replay or stop treating a game as an intention; keep/remove or clarify a game's role; correct a stale rating or fitness model; recognize an intentional exception; change future buying. Useful prompts may include highly valued but neglected games, long-unplayed purchases, prediction surprises, possible role duplication, and unusual games with an unclear role. The system should surface the question and evidence, not automatically recommend buying, selling, or changing weights. It must be valid to report that nothing needs attention. Start with brainstorming/decision discovery, then produce the specification in shelf-judge-1q2.2; do not implement UI or metrics during this bead.
close_reason: Decision framework completed in .lore/work/brainstorm/collection-profile-decision-taxonomy.md. Owner selected current-fitness ratings for mechanics, designers, and artists as the first identity answer and explicit play intentions as the first attention family. Fresh-context review found the artifact sufficient input for shelf-judge-1q2.2.

title: Support manual Play Time and Player Count values
description: Replace the current score-override behavior for the derived Play Time and Player Count axes with manual overrides of the underlying values used in calculations. A user should be able to provide corrected or missing Play Time and Player Count data when they disagree with BoardGameGeek or BGG lacks sufficient data. The overridden values must drive both the corresponding derived-axis calculations and the Purchase Utilization system. Decide and document whether these inputs belong directly in the derived-axis system or in a shared source-data/manual-override layer, while preserving clear precedence between manual values and BGG data.
design: Prefer a single effective-value resolution path shared by derived-axis scoring and Purchase Utilization; do not duplicate override handling in each consumer. Keep the architecture open to other user-correctable source values if the existing model supports that evolution.
acceptance_criteria: Manual Play Time and Player Count inputs override the underlying BGG/source values, rather than merely overriding the resulting 1-10 scores. Derived Play Time and Player Count scores are calculated from the effective overridden values. Purchase Utilization uses the same effective Play Time and Player Count values. Behavior is defined when only one axis is overridden, when values are missing from BGG, and when manual overrides are cleared. Existing score calculation behavior remains unchanged when no manual overrides are present. Automated tests cover override precedence, derived-axis calculations, Purchase Utilization, missing BGG data, and clearing overrides.
notes: User need: Play Time and Player Count currently allow overriding the derived score, but users need to override the input values used for calculation. P1 priority.

title: Collection Profile: Identity and Attention
description: Redesign the profile page to answer two user questions: What does my collection reveal about me? What deserves my attention or a decision now? Begin with the decisions and understanding the page must support, not with available metrics. Descriptive statistics may remain when they help users verify their taste model, such as axis distributions. An attention item must identify a concrete unresolved question and plausible response; crossing a statistical threshold is not sufficient.
design: Treat the page as a stable identity view plus a small decision inbox. Separate descriptive orientation, model diagnostics, and collection decisions. Audit every existing section against a named user question. Retain, demote to drilldown, redesign, or remove it based on usefulness. Prediction misses are a candidate model diagnostic, not a committed feature. Do not implement new metrics before the product spec establishes the question they answer and what a user could do with the result.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed product specification defines the two headline questions, the concrete decision taxonomy, and the evidence needed to raise each kind of attention item before implementation begins; every prominent item maps to an understandable unresolved question and at least one plausible user response; existing profile content is explicitly classified as retain, drilldown, redesign, or remove, including axis distributions, Tournament divergence, collection outliers, prediction residuals, and purchase utilization; descriptive statistics support collection identity or model verification without being presented as decisions; the page can honestly show that nothing currently needs attention; unsupported urgency and metrics-first insights are prohibited; implementation requirements cover applicable daemon, web, persistence, accessibility, mobile, automated, and browser validation.

title: Trusted Collection Insights
description: Make collection-profile insights credible enough to deserve attention. Define a common evidence and confidence model, then audit preference divergence, axis suggestions, and collection outliers against it. Repair, replace, remove, or reject signals that are self-referential, statistically weak, poorly explained, or unsupported by sufficient data. Insights must distinguish observations from interpretations and expose the games and measurements behind each claim. The resulting contract also governs subsequent collection insights such as value earned.
design: Treat divergence, suggestions, and outliers as consumers of a shared insight-quality contract rather than independent dashboard curiosities. The epic may conclude that an existing signal should be removed. Prefer transparent deterministic evidence over additional inference.
acceptance_criteria: Profile insights carry concrete evidence, significance/confidence or sample-sufficiency information, and an explanation of why they are notable; tournament preference diagnostics no longer compare a signal against a fitness score containing that same signal; axis suggestions require evidence that an attribute affects preference rather than mere concentration or variance; outliers have collection-appropriate detection and understandable comparisons; weak insights can be suppressed or retired; deterministic tests cover retained insight rules and abstention cases; the evidence contract is concrete enough for downstream epics to apply without inventing presentation-only credibility heuristics.
close_reason: All children complete; trusted insight evidentiary integrity accepted with explicit product-value limitation

title: Collection Value-Earned Insight
description: Determine whether purchase and usage data can support a trustworthy collection value-earned insight, then deliver the approved data, calculation, and product surfaces before the home-page brief is designed. Identify the user question this metric should answer; evaluate purchase price, play count, duration, player count, and fitness as possible inputs; and test whether the result is useful rather than merely numerically elaborate. The existing quality-adjusted social-hour formula is a hypothesis, not a committed design. Compare it with simpler measures such as cost per play and cost per player-hour, and account for missing or ambiguous data including gifts, used purchases, expansions, zero-play games, changing player counts, and uncertain play duration.
design: Start with a decision gate before implementation. Keep factual utilization measures separate from subjective value judgments. Do not make purchase price required until missing-data behavior and the benefit of that burden are validated. Evaluate whether fitness adjustment double-counts preference, whether player-count weighting has a defensible meaning, and whether a configurable hourly target adds insight or arbitrary precision. Any retained output must satisfy the Trusted Collection Insights evidence, confidence, explainability, and abstention model. Decompose approved implementation into child issues covering data/persistence, calculation, API/clients, presentation, migration, and validation.
acceptance_criteria: A documented go/no-go decision states which user question the insight answers and whether it belongs on the collection brief; candidate formulas are compared on representative games and sensitivity to each input; data provenance, optionality, missing-value semantics, currency assumptions, and edge cases are defined; required versus optional collection fields and migration implications are decided; if approved, a specification and dependency-ordered child issues implement and validate the selected metric across applicable daemon, web, and CLI surfaces; retained outputs expose understandable evidence and abstain when inputs are insufficient; if rejected, the epic records why the concept would be misleading or not useful and no implementation is required.

title: Grade player-count fit by range distance
description: Replace the binary playerCountFit 10/1 result with the approved distance model: in-range subtract the larger endpoint delta from 10; out-of-range subtract both endpoint deltas; clamp to 1-10. Update tests and derived-axis specification.
design: For target T and valid bounds m..M: if m <= T <= M, score clamp(10 - max(T-m, M-T)); otherwise score clamp(10 - (abs(T-m) + abs(T-M))). Higher-is-better remains identity on the native 1-10 scale.
